To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ADEPT Concept-based Digital Learning Environment is an integrated digital library and digital learning environment that provides a set of services for the creation, searching, and presentation of knowledge bases (KB) of strongly structured concepts, digital library collections of information objects, and collections of presentations materials, such as lecture notes, that are organized and presented as trajectories through the knowledge bases.
the use of concept-based digital libraries is an effective way to teach scientific concepts.

the DLE is an effective and efficient means for teaching and learning in undergraduate science courses, and that its design is based on the following assumptions: (1) that learning is facilitated when learning material is organized, accessed, and presented at the granularity of appropriate sets or networks of scientific concepts; and (2) that learning is enhanced when students are given the opportunity to create and use their own learning materials, and to share them with their peers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a DLE that supports the use of conceptually structured learning environments.

the design and development of a digital learning environment (DLE) in which learning is facilitated through explicit organization, access and presentation of learning materials at the granularity of appropriate sets (KBs) and their interrelationships of scientific concepts.

the design and development of a DLE that facilitates the creation, search, retrieval and display of knowledge bases of scientific concepts, digital library collections organized by the concepts of those knowledge bases, and presentation materials, such a lectures and laboratory materials that are organized as a trajectory through the concepts of a knowledge base.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this DLE provides the means to create and access a knowledge-based digital environment that is designed to support concept-based learning and research in the sciences and engineering.

the ADEPT DLE is a successful and effective environment for the teaching of introductory science courses, and that its success is due in significant part to its concept-based approach to the organization of both the learning materials and the information resources.

we have created an integrated DLE that supports the creation, search and display of knowledge bases of scientific concepts and the collections of information objects and presentation materials that are organized and accessible by these concepts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DLE supports the development and application of concept-based digital learning environments.

the DLE provides the following: a knowledge base of concepts that are used to describe and organize information objects, presentation materials, and learning activities; an interface to a collection of information objects that is organized and accessible by concepts; an interface to the presentation of learning materials that is organized by concepts; and an interface to a set of learning activities that are organized by concepts.

we have designed and built a system for the organization, access, and presentation of learning materials at the concept level, and we have demonstrated its effectiveness in a variety of undergraduate science courses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DLE can be used in a way that is complementary to the traditional lecture and laboratory-based approaches to teaching science.
the DLE can be used as a platform for the creation and delivery of digital educational resources.
a concept-based DLE provides a flexible, scalable, and powerful environment for supporting the creation and delivery of learning materials that are organized around the concepts that define a domain.
